sections.text:
Controllability asks whether inputs can drive the state to any value in finite time. Form the controllability matrix M = [B AB ... A^(n−1)B]. The system is controllable when M has rank n. Observability asks whether the state can be found from outputs; form O = [C; CA; ...; CA^(n−1)], and rank n means observable.

Pole placement uses u = −Kx so that A − BK has chosen eigenvalues. If controllable, K exists. An observer estimates x from y: xhatdot = Axhat + Bu + L(y − Cxhat). The error e = x − xhat obeys edot = (A − LC)e, so choose L to make A − LC fast and stable.

sections.heading: Optimal and robust
sections.text:
Optimal control balances performance against effort. The linear quadratic regulator (LQR) minimises J = integral (x^T Q x + u^T R u) dt for xdot = Ax + Bu. Q and R are positive definite weights. The feedback u = −Kx uses K = R^-1 B^T P, where P solves the algebraic Riccati equation. Larger Q penalises state error; larger R penalises control effort.

Robust control designs for plant uncertainty and disturbances, often with H∞ methods, which bound the worst-case amplification of disturbances. Nonlinear control handles saturation, friction or large swings, for example by feedback linearisation or sliding mode.

sections.heading: Digital implementation
sections.text: Digital implementation samples the plant and computes the controller at fixed intervals. Sampling adds delay, so choose a sample time well below the dominant time constant, and check aliasing, quantisation and actuator limits.

keyPoints: State-space form is xdot = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du, and the eigenvalues of A are the poles.
A system is controllable if [B AB ... A^(n−1)B] has rank n, and observable if [C; CA; ...; CA^(n−1)] has rank n.
Pole placement sets the eigenvalues of A − BK by choosing K, and an observer sets those of A − LC by choosing L.
LQR minimises J = integral (x^T Q x + u^T R u) dt and uses u = −Kx with K = R^-1 B^T P.
Robust control allows for model uncertainty, while nonlinear control handles effects such as saturation and friction.
Digital control needs a sample time short enough for the loop, plus checks on delay, aliasing and quantisation.

en.title: Advanced electromagnetic theory and computational methods
en.short: Maxwell’s equations, boundary conditions, waveguides, radiation and FDM, FEM and MoM solvers.

sections.heading: Maxwell’s equations
sections.text:
Four equations link E (electric field, V/m), B (magnetic flux density, T), D (electric flux density, C/m²) and H (magnetic field strength, A/m). In differential form: ∇·D = ρ, ∇·B = 0, ∇×E = −∂B/∂t, ∇×H = J + ∂D/∂t. Applying the divergence theorem and Stokes theorem turns these into the integral form, which is what you use for flux through a closed surface or emf around a loop.

At an interface, tangential E is continuous, tangential H is continuous if there is no surface current, normal B is continuous, and normal D jumps by the surface charge density. These boundary conditions let you match solutions in two media.

sections.heading: Waveguides and radiation
sections.text:
In a hollow rectangular waveguide of broad dimension a, the dominant TE10 mode has cutoff frequency fc = c ÷ (2a). Below fc the wave does not propagate.

Example: a = 22.86 mm gives fc = 3×10⁸ ÷ (2 × 0.02286) = 6.56 GHz.

Radiation comes from accelerating charge. In the far field, power density falls as 1/r², so field strength falls as 1/r. Antenna pattern and gain describe how the radiated power is directed.

sections.heading: Numerical methods
sections.text:
Finite difference (FDM) replaces derivatives with differences on a regular grid: simple and fast, but weak at curved boundaries. Finite element (FEM) splits the region into triangles or tetrahedra and solves a weak form: good for complex shapes and mixed materials. The method of moments (MoM) solves integral equations for surface currents using Green’s functions, and suits open radiating structures.

Explicit time stepping is stable only if the Courant condition holds. In three dimensions on a uniform grid, Δt ≤ Δx ÷ (c√3). With Δx = 1 mm: Δt ≤ 1×10⁻³ ÷ (3×10⁸ × 1.732) = 1.92 ps.

keyPoints: Tangential E is always continuous across an interface; tangential H is continuous if there is no surface current; normal B is continuous.
Rectangular waveguide TE10 cutoff: fc = c ÷ (2a).
Far-field power density falls as 1/r² and field strength as 1/r.
FDM suits regular grids, FEM suits complex geometry, MoM suits open radiators.
Explicit time stepping on a uniform 3D grid needs Δt ≤ Δx ÷ (c√3).

en.title: Research methods and dissertation
en.short: Research question, literature review, research design, ethics, analysis and dissertation writing.

sections.heading: Research question
sections.text:
A master’s project starts with a question, not a broad topic. A topic names an area; a research question asks something answerable with evidence. Narrow it by population, variable, setting and time. A good question is focused, feasible, relevant and ethical. Test it by asking whether you can collect or simulate the data within your time and resources.

Example: instead of 'solar power in Nigeria', ask 'How does battery capacity affect the unmet load (demand not supplied) of a 20 kW solar mini-grid serving a clinic in Ogun State over one year?' This names the system, variable, setting and period.

sections.heading: Review and design
sections.text:
A literature review is a critical synthesis of what is known, not a list of summaries. Search databases, read primary sources, and state the gap your question addresses. Record your searches.

Research design is the plan that links your question to evidence. An experiment manipulates variables under controlled conditions. A simulation uses a computational model when experiments are costly, slow or unsafe. Simulation results need verification (does the code solve the equations correctly?) and validation (does the model match reality?).

Ethical approval is permission from a research ethics committee before collecting data from people, animals or personal records. Rules differ by country and institution. In Nigeria, university ethics committees handle most student projects, and health research may need national health research ethics approval. Check your institution’s rules.

sections.heading: Analysis and writing
sections.text:
Plan the analysis before data collection. Quantitative work uses descriptive statistics, uncertainty estimates and, where justified, significance tests. Simulation work needs sensitivity checks. Qualitative work uses coding to group repeated ideas.

Technical writing is plain, precise and reproducible. Report what you did, why, what you found and what limits the findings. A master’s dissertation has a title page, abstract, introduction, literature review, method, results, discussion, conclusion, references and appendices. The format is set by your university; follow its handbook.

keyPoints: A research question names a population, variable, setting and time, and must be answerable with available evidence.
A literature review synthesises primary sources and identifies the gap the project addresses.
Research design links the question to evidence; experiments manipulate variables, while simulations need verification and validation.
Ethical approval must be obtained before collecting data from people, animals or personal records, and rules differ by country and institution.
Plan the data analysis before collection, including uncertainty and sensitivity checks where relevant.
A master’s dissertation normally follows the structure set by the university handbook, from abstract through method, results, discussion and references.
